catalog_quote: Suprasegments Tone: Zou language has three contrastive tones. They are: 1. Level, 2. Low-rising, and 3. Falling. Level tone is unmarked, others are marked in ´, ` respectively as in the following: 1. 1 Level : hai “mango” 2. Low-rising : ha´i “chew, masticate/skim off” 3. Falling : ha`i “cup/forget” 2. 1. Level : sa “hot” 2. Low-rising : sa´ “meat” 3. Falling : sa` “dense, thick” ... Conclusion: This paper briefly shows some phonological features of Zou language. ... It is a tonal language having three degree of tones: level, low-rising, and falling.

audit.action: cite a better source for the same coding
audit.reasoning: (1) Quote check: both halves of the deciding quotation are verbatim in the held PDF at the stated places (Suprasegments PDF p.16, Conclusion PDF p.17); 'stress'/'accent' absent from the article as claimed. (2) The deciding source is a short 2013 descriptive phonology article; Glottolog lists two PhD reference grammars that outrank it. Both were fetched sources now from Shodhganga (the earlier session's timeouts were the port-8443 redirect; a Referer header bypasses it). Lukram 2013 ch.2 p.36 gives an explicit 'Stress –... stress, rhythm are not found in this language' plus the same three-tone analysis (its sec. 2.4 is the article's tone section verbatim). Tungdim 2012 ch.4 (JNU, Praat-based) independently analyses Zo as a syllable-TBU tone language with four lexical tones and has no stress/accent section in 767 pp. (3) Coding 'tonal, no word-stress rule, domain unstated' is therefore confirmed

sources.quote: p.251: 'the Tone Bearing Unit ... is the "syllable" in Zo ... Zo is monosyllabic, partially agglutinating tone language. The Zo tones are treated as Suprasegmental features in this study.' p.263: 'My analysis of Zo tones produces, 4 (four) underlying lexical tones in isolation ... High Rising tone(H), High Falling tone(L), Mid or Level tone(M) and a slightly Low tone' (the Low tone illustrated only on checked syllables: kəp 'cry', nət 'illness'); p.265 Table 30 minimal quadruplets sa: 'meat' (Rising) / sa: 'hot' (Level) / sa: 'thick' (Falling) — the same triplet our record quotes — and 'tone o
sources.locator: p.251 (4.3.3), pp.263-265 (4.4, Table 30 'Four contrastive lexical tones in Zo'), p.286-288 (4.4.4-4.4.6 compound tones, neutralization, Tone Rules); table of contents pp. x-xiv
sources.note: Largest grammar of the language with a 40-page instrumental (Praat) tonology; independent author/institution confirms tone-only word prosody (4 tones incl. a checked Low tone vs the article's 3) and documents first-syllable reduction in compounds; no stress section in 767 pp.
